AR-2026F-SR8.aiSummary: The resolution would have let lawmakers introduce a bill to charge digital asset mining businesses fees for extra electrical power use and add oversight rules. It would affect mining businesses already running and new ones that start after the law’s effective date. The money would go to state agencies for monitoring and enforcement work.

AR-2026F-SR39.aiSummary: The Senate adopted a resolution to honor Arkansas public servants and to observe Public Service Recognition Week from May 3 through May 9, 2026. It recognizes the work of state, local, and federal public workers in areas like teaching, health, elections, safety, and infrastructure. The resolution also calls on people in Arkansas to acknowledge their service.

AR-2026F-SR20.aiSummary: A Senate resolution would authorize the introduction of a bill to change the Industrial Development Authorities Expansion Act. The bill would change who can serve on an industrial development authority board, allow some board members to be removed for good cause, and say these authorities must follow local zoning and planning rules. It would also change rules for acquiring property and say the act takes effect right away if approved.

AR-2026F-SR11.aiSummary: The resolution would let lawmakers introduce a bill that would require digital asset miners and digital asset mining businesses to give written notice before buying or leasing land or a building, or before starting construction. The notice would go to the Arkansas Public Service Commission and the local government where the work is planned. It would apply to projects for digital asset mining or for using a blockchain network.

AR-2026F-SB4.aiSummary: The bill sets money and staff limits for several Arkansas Department of Health licensing and regulation boards for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It covers boards such as acupuncture, alcoholism and drug abuse counseling, athletic training, chiropractic examiners, counseling, dental examiners, and dietetics. The funds would pay for salaries, office costs, travel, and other operating expenses for those boards.

AR-2026F-HB1064.aiSummary: The bill would set aside money for the Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration to pay for a range of state programs in fiscal year 2026-2027. It includes funds for interstate groups, state pay items, grants, pension and relief funds, disaster aid, unemployment claims, and court cost refunds. It also sets money for child abuse and domestic violence services, justice programs, the Arkansas Sheriffs' Association, and drug enforcement and education.

AR-2026F-HB1055.aiSummary: Act 126 sets the state budget for the Department of Education’s Office of Early Childhood for fiscal year 2026-2027. It funds salaries, office costs, grants, and related work, including $14,635,808 for operations, $188,667,976 in federal money, $9,000,000 for child care program grants, and $200,000 for childcare facility grants. The act takes effect on July 1, 2026.
